summary: This chest X-ray shows a large rounded air pocket with a fluid level sitting behind the heart, in the lower chest area. This appearance is often seen when part of the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm into the chest (called a hiatal hernia) or when the stomach becomes very distended with air. It is not a lung problem itself, but it can sometimes cause symptoms like heartburn, bloating, or chest discomfort. Further imaging, such as a CT scan or a barium swallow study, would help confirm exactly what this structure is and whether treatment is needed. The rest of the visible lung tissue does not show signs of infection or fluid buildup, though the image quality makes a full assessment somewhat limited.
